task_brief: Listening work on active listening. primary_task: Target for this guided_b session: Practice active listening with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support. Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of active listening. Check, revise, or improve work about active listening using stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about active listening; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. What active listening means here: Timbre is sound quality—the set of audible features that helps two sources or actions sound different even at a similar pitch and loudness. How the relationship changes the result: The material and action shape a sound’s beginning, continuation, and ending. A quick tap has a sharp attack and short decay; rubbed paper has a softer attack and continuing noise. 1. Guided practice: Begin the second pass on active listening with the earlier model and cue closed. Make two new studies, compare them with the first supported pass, and report whether the previously fragile move now holds without the prompt. 2. Independent transfer: Transfer active listening to a third, unfamiliar case without reopening the scaffold. Revisit the move marked fragile in the first pass and cite the independent evidence that shows whether it now works. 3. Critique: Describe before judging. Locate evidence, compare it with the maker’s stated intent, ask one genuine question, and offer options; the maker keeps final authority. A private self-critique receives full credit. 4. Reflection: Compare an earlier and later state. Name the choice that changed, cite what became visible, audible, notated, or workable, and state the next revision or reason to keep the result. Your choices remain yours: Different safe household sound or supplied event-map route, comparison order, quality words supported by evidence, layer to foreground, final listening or production revision choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about active listening. ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g4-arts-music-u03-l06

Lesson focus: active listening

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD B — support-fading pass for active listening. Earlier-pass substitute: Tap a tabletop once, then rub one sheet of paper for the same count. Map each as ATTACK → SUSTAIN → DECAY and cite the moment that distinguishes them. A trusted adult may produce the two sounds if needed. Mark the relationship involving attack as the fragile move, then hide this resource. Make two new studies, loops, maps, or responses without the prompt. Reopen only afterward; compare the order of decisions and the evidence. Report whether the fragile move held. If it did not, use the criteria to name the mismatch without changing the learner’s intent or copying the example. Use it to study active listening; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: The submission contains the required work blocks and one reviewable process state; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
The learner locates relevant attack, sustain, decay, brightness, density, register, layer, and source action and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Tap, point through, gesture, or use the supplied notation or event map without recording. A written or notated response can show structure and reasoning; it does not claim hearing or performed control that was not actually demonstrated. No instrument, microphone, camera, or public performance is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses sound (active listening). You do not have to hear it to do it. You may use a written or drawn version, feel the beat by tapping or watching, or read the notes on paper instead.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.fallback: Count, point through, tap, speak, gesture, or read the complete pulse and pitch map silently; no instrument, speaker, microphone, or recording is required.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce active listening to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one attack relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact attack evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from attack, sustain, decay, brightness, density, register, layer, and source action; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply active listening under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on active listening rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_instruction.title: What active listening means here
concept_instruction.body: Timbre is sound quality—the set of audible features that helps two sources or actions sound different even at a similar pitch and loudness.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: The material and action shape a sound’s beginning, continuation, and ending. A quick tap has a sharp attack and short decay; rubbed paper has a softer attack and continuing noise.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: A dense mix can feel full but mask individual layers. A sparse texture reveals timbre clearly but may reduce weight or momentum. Worked example: Tap a tabletop once, then rub one sheet of paper for the same count. Map each as ATTACK → SUSTAIN → DECAY and cite the moment that distinguishes them. A trusted adult may produce the two sounds if needed. Non-example: Calling one source “better” or naming an instrument family without citing an audible or supplied source feature is preference or recall, not listening evidence.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for active listening is present, but the record does not yet locate attack, sustain, decay, brightness, density, register, layer, and source action that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
